claim: Delta N-gram keeps the pretrained N-gram table T0 fixed and writes evidence into a sparse patch Delta, so T = T0 + Delta and every row with Delta_j = 0 reads exactly its pretrained value; clearing Delta returns the original model.
stance_target: The repo's Memory Grafting claim that frozen Engram tables can be treated as immutable capacity that costs no optimizer state
scope_conditions: Hashed N-gram table read at every position through H hash heads; patch nonzero only on written rows
quoted_support: We write the table as T = T0 + Delta, where T0 is the pretrained table and Delta is a patch that is nonzero only on rows that have been written. Every row with Delta_j = 0 reads exactly its pretrained value.

claim: The memory state carries no optimizer state at all — it stores only written row ids, patches and write counts — so a frozen table costs its bf16 rows and nothing else.
stance_target: The repo's 16 B/trainable-param memory math, in which frozen params cost only their bf16 weight (2 B) and no Adam state or gradient
scope_conditions: Delta N-gram memory state design; forward-only write path
quoted_support: The state stores only rows that have been written: their row ids, patches Delta_j and write counts c_j, plus a block clock with the bookkeeping for lazy decay. It carries no optimizer state.

claim: At use time, writing requires forward passes only: no backpropagation, no optimizer and no labels, and no weight is changed.
stance_target: The repo's claim that frozen memory adds capacity without adding per-token FLOPs or training cost
scope_conditions: Delta N-gram inference-time write path; the writer and D1 delta rule are identical at training and use time, training only adds a backward pass
quoted_support: At use time evidence is written as it arrives and queries read T0 + Delta, with no backpropagation, no optimizer and no change to any weight.

claim: The entire trainable component in the Delta N-gram design is a 4,075,681-parameter writer; the 48-layer, 512-expert backbone, the read-out and T0 are all frozen.
stance_target: The repo's claim that a 7B-total / ~1B-trainable design is reachable, and the stronger version that trainable budget can be far below 1B if the memory subsystem is frozen
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 48 layers, 512 routed experts with ten active per token
quoted_support: Backbone, read-out and T0 are frozen; the writer (4,075,681 parameters) is the only trained component.

claim: Delta N-gram's own writer training used expert parallelism 4 alongside data parallelism 4 on four H200 GPUs, so the published recipe depends on the exact topology the CMP 170HX's no-P2P fabric rules out.
stance_target: The repo's claim that EP is ruled out on this box while frozen-table designs remain reproducible; the strongest frozen-table paper trains with EP4
scope_conditions: Native-model writer training: four H200 GPUs, EP=4, DP=4, 12 complete trajectories per update
quoted_support: We train on four H200 GPUs with expert parallelism 4 and data parallelism 4. Each update uses 12 complete trajectories and backpropagates through the whole write chain of each.

claim: On a 0.6B prototype trained with a question-answering objective, the forward-only writer keeps 16 of 16 facts after a second write, where online gradient writes into the same table keep only 2-4 of 16.
stance_target: The claim that forward-only writes into frozen memory are more stable than gradient writes into the same rows
scope_conditions: Qwen3-0.6B-Base prototype, 2,000 synthetic episodes, 16 held-out worlds with two writes each; baseline is ten SparseAdam steps per evidence block at lr 0.01 or 0.05
quoted_support: On a 0.6B prototype trained with a question-answering objective, the writer keeps 16 of 16 facts after a second write, where online gradient writes into the same table keep 2-4.

claim: The binding is tied to the trained question form: a paraphrased question that still names the entity stays at the empty-memory 2/16 level, because the rows such queries read overlap the written rows in only about 6% of positions.
stance_target: The implication that frozen-table writes generalize to unseen phrasings; retrieval is exact-hash-address bound
scope_conditions: 0.6B prototype, transfer probes without retraining
quoted_support: Asked with a paraphrased question that still names the entity, the writer stays at the empty-memory 2/16 before and after writing. The rows read by such queries overlap the written rows in only about 6% of positions.

claim: Write chains erode stored facts: four writes leave 60 of 64 facts answerable, and after sixteen writes 46 of 64 are answered right after their own write but only 19 at the end.
stance_target: The claim that frozen memory accumulates knowledge monotonically across a long training or use chain
scope_conditions: 0.6B prototype, chains of 4 and 16 writes, no retraining
quoted_support: Without retraining, four writes leave 60 of 64 facts answerable. After sixteen writes, 46 of 64 are answered right after their own write but only 19 at the end.

claim: On 64 held-out late-2025 news events, the plain writer lowers continuation NLL by 0.068 nats/token against empty memory and by 0.024 against another document's memory, and by 0.063 and 0.013 after 16 intervening articles.
stance_target: The claim that frozen-table memory yields a measurable, document-specific gain rather than a null result
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, writer trained to 100M target tokens on raw text; 64 held-out news events
quoted_support: on 64 held-out news events it lowers continuation NLL by 0.068 nats/token against empty memory and by 0.024 against another document's memory, and 0.063 and 0.013 after 16 intervening articles.

claim: The delta writer's memory is more document-specific than the plain writer's and retains 70% of that specificity after 16 distractors versus 54%, at the cost of a smaller total gain over empty memory.
stance_target: Whether reading current memory while encoding is worth the sequential-write cost
scope_conditions: Delta writer forked from the alpha=1 checkpoint at 80M and trained to 100M; 64 news events with 16 intervening articles
quoted_support: The delta writer's memory is more specific to its document (Delta_donor 0.032 against 0.023 without distractors) and keeps more of that specificity after 16 distractors (70% against 54%); its total gain over empty memory on these news events is smaller.

claim: Both writers completed 35,000 consecutive writes on two hardware stacks without numerical failure, including the delta writer whose encoding feeds back through its own memory.
stance_target: The claim that forward-only frozen-table writes are numerically stable over long chains
scope_conditions: Seven-task chain of the prior Representation Drift work; H200 and A800 stacks
quoted_support: Both writers, including the delta writer whose encoding feeds back through its own memory, made 35,000 consecutive writes on two hardware stacks without numerical failure.

claim: Learned-task accuracy changes by only -0.26pp (plain) and -0.52pp (delta) over the rest of a seven-task chain, against -7.29pp for Adam table updates into the same rows.
stance_target: The claim that frozen-base-plus-sparse-patch writes cause far less catastrophic forgetting than gradient writes into the table
scope_conditions: Seven-task chain; comparison against the Adam table-update arm of the prior Representation Drift paper (reused, not rerun)
quoted_support: After each task is written, learned-task accuracy changes by -0.26pp (plain) and -0.52pp (delta) over the rest of the chain, against -7.29pp for the Adam table updates.

claim: Net acquisition on tasks the writer never saw is negative (-12/448) and recall of written examples is only 23-25%, so frozen-table writes preserve stability at the cost of almost no new capability.
stance_target: The repo's framing that frozen Engram tables are 'the cheapest capacity available' — they are cheap, but they do not by themselves add capability
scope_conditions: Seven-task chain, 448 support examples (64 per task), final memory state
quoted_support: Net acquisition on these tasks, which the writer never saw, is negative (-12/448), and recall of written examples is 23-25%.

claim: General-input big-K drift is 32.8%, 1.6x the Adam baseline's 20.75%, and it concentrates in eight format bigram rows that every example writes, whose patches reach 4.4-11.7x their T0 norm.
stance_target: The assumption that freezing the base table eliminates drift; drift moves to the patch and concentrates on hot rows
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, general-input probes; big-K drift metric inherited from the Representation Drift paper
quoted_support: General-input big-K drift is 32.8%, 1.6 times that of [31]. It enters at the injection layer through eight format bigram rows that every example writes, whose patches reach 4.4-11.7 times T0.

claim: Zeroing the eight hot format rows removes over 98% of the layer-2 drift on math inputs — and also removes their NLL gain, so drift and gain are carried by the same rows and cannot be separated by row surgery.
stance_target: Whether row-level attribution gives a usable knob for trading drift against gain in frozen-table designs
scope_conditions: Post-hoc row zeroing experiment on the final memory state; equivalence proof that zeroing a row set equals never committing it
quoted_support: Zeroing eight such rows removes over 98% of layer-2 drift on math inputs, together with their NLL gain.

claim: The native memory read-out on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses H=16 hash heads (eight bigram, eight trigram) with row width d=160, concatenated into R^2560 and injected into the residual stream before layer-2 attention.
stance_target: The concrete shape of the Engram-style memory injection the repo would have to implement
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next native N-gram table
quoted_support: On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, H = 16 (bigram and trigram, eight heads each) and each row has d = 160 dimensions. The read-out concatenates the 16 rows and injects the result into the residual stream before the attention of layer 2.

claim: The 0.6B prototype used an external zero-initialised table of 16,384 rows each for bigrams and trigrams with row width 1024 and 1,190,465 writer parameters, injected before decoder layer 1.
stance_target: The smallest viable frozen-table configuration for a from-scratch small model on this box
scope_conditions: Prototype stage on Qwen3-0.6B-Base / post-trained Qwen3-0.6B
quoted_support: a frozen 0.6B model with an external, zero-initialised hash table (T0 = 0): 16,384 rows each for bigrams and trigrams, row width 1024.

claim: The writer's training corpus mixes Stack v2 Edu 20%, arXiv 25%, Project Gutenberg 20%, FineWeb-Edu 15%, CC-News 17.5% and same-event CC-News streams 2.5% across 38,566 documents.
stance_target: Overlap with the run's own 75/15/10 FineWeb-Edu / Stack-Edu / FineMath mix, useful as a cross-check on data-pipeline design
scope_conditions: Raw-text writer training data, six streams, target-token share
quoted_support: Raw English text and source code from six streams, mixed by target-token share: code from Stack v2 Edu (20%), arXiv papers (25%) and Project Gutenberg books (20%) from the Common Pile, FineWeb-Edu web pages (15%), CC-News articles (17.5%), and time-ordered streams of several CC-News reports on the same event (2.5%).

claim: An optional lazy decay pulls the patch toward zero, i.e. the table toward T0 (Delta_j <- alpha*Delta_j), giving reversible forgetting rather than the zero-pull decay of Gated DeltaNet and KDA.
stance_target: The claim that a frozen base table makes forgetting reversible, a property gradient-updated tables lack
scope_conditions: Delta N-gram Section 3.5 memory state and decay design
quoted_support: ours pulls the patch toward zero and hence the table toward T0: Delta_j <- alpha*Delta_j, i.e. T_j <- T0_j + alpha(T_j - T0_j). It is applied lazily.

claim: Accuracy was measured on A800 GPUs with vLLM using a separate FP32 patch branch, while NLL and representations were measured on H200 GPUs with the native training stack; the two states differ by 4-6% from cross-stack numerics.
stance_target: Whether the paper's numbers transfer to a GA100/SM80 box with no FP8 and a different numerics stack
scope_conditions: Two-machine evaluation protocol; each machine writes its own chain from an empty state
quoted_support: Accuracy is measured on A800 GPUs with vLLM, whose Qwen3.8 read-out we extend with a separate FP32 patch branch. NLL and representations are measured on H200 GPUs with the native training stack. Each machine writes its own chain from an empty state, and the two states differ by 4-6% because of cross-stack numerics.
